column3: The Hebrew uses a singular feminine singing verb before naming Deborah and Barak and ends with “saying”; BSB uses a plural subject and supplies “this song.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “I”; BSB states it once in each singing clause without that initial repetition.
The Hebrew repeats the dripping verb for both heavens and clouds; BSB has “poured out rain” and “poured down water,” supplying “rain” in the first clause.
The Hebrew says the mountains “flowed” and explicitly says “this Sinai”; BSB has “quaked” and “the One of Sinai.”
The Hebrew repeats “ways” for the deserted and crooked routes; BSB distinguishes “highways” and “byways.”
The Hebrew repeats “I arose”; BSB states Deborah’s arising once.
The Hebrew uses a singular choosing verb with an unnamed subject; BSB has plural “they.”

The Hebrew says to “speak a song” and repeats the captivity root in verb and noun; BSB has “sing a song” and “take hold of your captives.”
The Hebrew has singular collective “a survivor”; BSB has plural “the survivors.”
The Hebrew names the “scribe’s staff”; BSB has “the marshal’s staff.”
The Hebrew uses a passive verb for being sent into the valley and explicitly names the heart in the final phrase; BSB has active “rushing” and “great indecision.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the heart in the phrase about Reuben’s deliberations; BSB says “great indecision.”
The Hebrew names “seas” in the plural; BSB says “the coast” without repeating that noun.
The Hebrew uses singular “his soul” and explicitly says “to die”; BSB has plural “their lives” and leaves the possibility of death implicit in “risked.”

The Hebrew repeats the galloping noun and uses singular collective “horse”; BSB has plural “horses” and says “mad galloping.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses passive blessing verbs; BSB describes Jael as “most blessed.”
The Hebrew says “a bowl of nobles”; BSB has “a magnificent bowl.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “her hand” and has plural “workers”; BSB begins with “She” and has singular “workman’s.”
The Hebrew twice says “between her feet”; BSB has “at her feet.” BSB also adds “still” to the statement that he lay down.
The Hebrew repeats the question word “why” and names the “steps” of the chariots; BSB has “Why” then “What” and uses “clatter.”
The Hebrew says “wise” without an explicit superlative and names “her words”; BSB has “wisest” and leaves the words implicit in “telling herself.”
The Hebrew calls the women a “womb, two wombs” and repeatedly names the spoil; BSB says “a girl or two” and condenses the repetitions.
